PullRequest.Title: chat: add a file chooser to the attachment menu
PullRequest.Body:

## Scenario

I have a file on my `~/Desktop`, such as a screenshot or a UI mockup, and want to attach it to a new chat's context. I should be able to pick it directly from VS Code without switching to Finder to drag it in, adding its folder to the workspace, or telling the agent to go find it.

The + menu offers Screenshot Window, but no explicit file chooser. Its workspace/history-based search makes files outside that scope difficult to discover, particularly in a new chat.

## Background

The attachment menu previously had a **Files & Folders...** entry, removed during the [context-picker refactor](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/248495). That entry searched workspace files and folders rather than opening a native file dialog; this change brings back an explicit file entry and adds a disk chooser for the scenario above.

Checked with Justin, the current area owner: there is no known specific reason for removing the entry, and he is happy to have it back.

## Changes

- Add **Files...** to Add Context, below **Agent...** and above **Open Editors** and **Screenshot Window** when those entries are available.
- Open the standard file dialog with multi-select, without requiring an existing workspace or session. Honor multi-selection in web and simplified dialogs too, preserving folder navigation and single-select/save behavior.
- Reuse attachment resolution, validate file and image support independently, report per-file failures, and restore input focus after completion or cancellation.
- Advertise existing file-attachment support for Agent Host. For image-only Cloud/remote targets, filter the chooser to images and preserve their embedded data, without introducing remote transfer of ordinary local files.
- Match image paste by leaving model-level handling to the existing attachment pipeline instead of adding a chooser-only model-vision rejection.
- Document the chooser in accessibility help, including Quick Chat, and cover the real dialog paths and capabilities with regression tests.

## How to Test

1. Start a new Agent Host chat, including one without a workspace.
2. Open **+ → Files...**, select a text file and a supported image from `~/Desktop`, and choose **Attach**. Both should appear as context and focus should return to the input.
3. Cancel the picker and verify that existing attachments are unchanged.
4. Try an image-only Cloud target with an image that also works via paste: **Files...** should offer images and attach the image data without a chooser-only model error. This does not add ordinary local-file transfer to Cloud.
5. With the simplified dialog enabled, use checkboxes or Space to select multiple files, then accept; folder navigation, single selection, and saving should keep working.
6. In Quick Chat, verify the chooser is available and included in accessibility help.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new loop, awaited caller, and transitive stat/read/hash/resize operations are directly traced, and the same resolver's existing multi-file drag/drop caller demonstrates that independent resources need not be serialized. Exact delay varies with file size and provider latency, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem stat/read operations, full image byte buffers, image hashing, decoding, canvas resizing, and encoding CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Critical-path time grows as the sum of work for all N selected files; for images it also grows with total selected bytes and pixel counts because each file completes its stat/read/hash/resize chain before the next starts.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased attachment latency and delayed return of focus after choosing multiple files, especially multiple screenshots or remote files
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no multi-select Files action on this menu; the existing equivalent multi-file attachment path for drag-and-drop resolves entries concurrently with Promise.all in chatDragAndDrop.ts.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new chooser accepts an arbitrary multi-selection but awaits resolveEditorAttachContext inside a for loop, serializing every selected resource before any attachments are committed and before the finally block restores input focus.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 176 is the per-resource `await this.attachmentResolveService.resolveEditorAttachContext({ resource })` newly placed inside the chooser's multi-select loop; RIGHT line 160 explicitly enables `canSelectMany: true`.
Findings.Title: Resolve selected attachments with bounded concurrency
Findings.Impact: Selecting several files makes the Add Context action wait for every file in series. Each image resolution performs filesystem stats, a full read, hashing, decode, and possible canvas resize/encode, so a realistic batch of screenshots incurs roughly the sum of all per-image delays rather than bounded parallel latency.
Findings.Evidence: The added line awaits resolveEditorAttachContext within `for (const resource of resources)`. That resolver calls fileService.stat; image resources then perform another stat, readFile, imageToHash, and resizeImage. `_handleContextPick` awaits this whole method before adding the returned entries, while the established multi-file drag/drop path calls the same resolver through Promise.all.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve selections through Promise.allSettled with a small shared concurrency limit, preserve input order, and emit the existing per-file notifications from settled results; this keeps memory/decoder pressure bounded while removing fully serial I/O and image processing.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The exact 2N call count, serial ordering, shared-parent duplication, and remote/simplified routing are all explicit in the code. Filesystem provider latency is environment-dependent, so magnitude varies, but the scaling mechanism and blocked accept path are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem provider stat calls, including remote filesystem IPC/network requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N checked items, acceptance now issues 2N stat calls in N sequential rounds; all items from one displayed folder redundantly stat that same parent N times.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased file-dialog acceptance latency and reduced responsiveness on remote or high-latency filesystem providers
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff the simplified dialog was single-select and acceptance validated at most one URI, causing one pair of parent/target stats.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Enabling canSelectMany adds a loop that awaits validate for each checked item sequentially. `validate` always performs parallel stats for the item's parent and target, but the next pair is not started until the prior pair completes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 602 introduces the awaited per-selected-item validation loop after RIGHT line 359 enables multi-selection; this raises the pre-diff maximum from one validation pair to N serialized pairs.
Findings.Title: Avoid serial re-stat of every checked item
Findings.Impact: In a remote/simplified dialog, checking a realistic batch of files and pressing Attach leaves the picker busy for N round trips, even though the directory listing already resolved those rows and every selected file commonly shares one parent. The delay scales linearly with selection count and remote latency before the dialog can close.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT lines 601-607 iterate selectedItems and await validate. `validate` calls `fileService.stat(dirname(uri))` and `fileService.stat(uri)` via Promise.allSettled. Browser non-file schemes and Electron remote schemes/settings route showOpenDialog through SimpleFileDialog, putting those provider calls on the accept critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Use an open-dialog multi-selection validator that groups items by parent, stats each parent once, and validates target URIs with a small concurrency limit; retain the current failure message and reject the selection if any target is invalid.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop/native Add Context > Files selecting multiple local files or screenshots
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The native dialog must return, then FileContextValuePick.asAttachment must resolve every selected URI before _handleContextPick commits any attachment; input focus is restored only after that entire resolution finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the native multi-select file dialog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC dialog operation per user invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new chat menu path did not exist; native showOpenDialog already supported multiSelections for other callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before attachment resolution begins

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each selected resource; for each image stat again and read the full file before hashing/resizing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least N stats; image selections add another N stats and N full reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The menu did not invoke this multi-file path; existing multi-resource drag/drop invokes the same resolver concurrently with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All operations are serialized across selected resources and block attachment commit/focus restoration

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N unique selected files; image cost further scales with aggregate bytes and pixel counts. There is no chooser-side cap, and attachment-model deduplication occurs only after all resolution work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One native dialog request; all N attachment resolutions are serialized by the added for/await loop. Within one image, stat/read/hash/resize stages are also awaited on its critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No resolution cache or in-flight coalescing is consulted. Even a URI already present in the attachment model is fully resolved before addContext later deduplicates it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serial loop and all transitive I/O/image work are explicit, and the awaited caller is traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on local storage speed and image dimensions; batches of screenshots are a realistic trigger, but no timing trace is available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the newly advertised multi-select action serializes independent heavyweight attachment resolutions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote or simplified file dialog selecting multiple files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog first lists the folder; after Attach, every checked row is validated before the dialog resolves, then chat attachment resolution runs before attachments appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/list the current directory to populate the simple picker
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The simplified dialog already listed the current folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before selection; unchanged by the multi-select accept logic

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the parent and target for each checked URI through the filesystem provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 2N provider calls in N serial rounds; the same parent is called N times for one-folder selections
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Single-selection acceptance validated at most one URI with two stats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Keeps the picker busy and prevents it from returning the selected URIs

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve selected chat attachments, including full image reads and processing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N resolver calls, with extra stat/read operations for images
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Files menu path existed; existing drag/drop batches equivalent independent resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after dialog validation and remains serialized before attachments are committed

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N checked files, commonly sharing one parent directory; subsequent attachment work scales with N files and selected image bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation executes N sequential rounds, each containing two parallel stats. Attachment resolution then executes N serial rounds. No limiter provides bounded overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The folder listing already resolved item metadata, but validation does not reuse it. Each item re-stats its identical parent, and there is no grouping, cache, or coalescing for those parent stats.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: routing to SimpleFileDialog for remote/non-file schemes or the simple-dialog setting and the exact validate call graph are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider round-trip latency varies substantially between local simplified mode, remote authorities, and virtual filesystems; the 2N call count and serial rounds do not.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: multi-selection adds serialized, redundant provider round trips, compounded by serialized attachment resolution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web File System Access picker selecting multiple local files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser picker returns handles; each handle is registered and persisted before showOpenDialog returns, after which chat resolves each URI before committing attachments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This implementation passed multiple:false and returned at most one handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks until user completes or cancels selection

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register and persist each selected FileSystemFileHandle in IndexedDB
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N registrations and up to N readwrite transactions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: showOpenDialog registered at most one selected file handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registrations are awaited serially before the dialog returns

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat/read registered handles and process images for attachment entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least N stats plus image-specific duplicate stats and N full reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat chooser path did not exist.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected browser file handles and aggregate selected image bytes/pixels.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One browser picker call; handle registrations are sequential, and chat attachment resolutions are also sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider keeps a handle map, but registerHandle still performs collision checks and an IndexedDB write per selected handle. Attachment resolution has no cache; warm handles avoid discovery but not stat/read work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and serialization; lower magnitude confidence for handle persistence overhead.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: IndexedDB transaction duration and typical browser selection counts are uncertain; that registration loop alone was not reported separately, while the heavier downstream serialized resolver is covered by a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: The attachment-resolution serialization is reportable. Sequential handle registration was considered but omitted as a separate finding because likely magnitude and safe batching semantics are less certain.

Scenarios.Scenario: Image-only Cloud/remote chat selecting multiple images
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The image-filtered dialog returns selected images; each image must be resolved into embedded data before attachments are added. No Cloud network request occurs during chooser resolution itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each selected image and produce embedded attachment data
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N full reads with two stats per image and N hash/resize operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud sessions exposed image support, but this new Files chooser path and its multi-selection were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks attachment creation and focus restoration until all images finish

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected images and their total file bytes/pixel dimensions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Image selection is multi-select, but image stat/read/hash/decode/resize work is serialized one image at a time by FileContextValuePick.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No image transformation cache or coalescing is used; embedded bytes are freshly read and transformed for every selection before model-level attachment handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: capability gating, image-only filter, embedded image path, and serial loop are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical image count and dimensions vary; common multi-screenshot selection is enough to expose additive latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the bounded-concurrency attachment finding; no separate network regression is introduced at selection time.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat startup/menu registration, capability advertisement, and accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution construction registers one additional context item and builds help text only when requested; capability metadata is read when configuring the widget/menu.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per contribution/widget/help invocation; not driven by file count until the user explicitly opens the chooser.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous expensive work is introduced on startup or menu rendering by these metadata/string changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache or retained collection is added; the registered pick is owned by the contribution disposable store.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code is constant-size registration, metadata, and localized text construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup, memory, rendering, or boundary regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and all diff pages. Two medium findings were submitted: serialized heavyweight attachment resolution for multi-select, and serialized redundant filesystem validation in the simplified dialog. Native/web registration, startup metadata, accessibility text, tests, cache behavior, and local/remote boundary paths were also assessed; no regression fix was identified.
